lead.title: Finland's Desentum hits the primary endpoint of its Phase 2 BASIT trial: ten weeks of injections relieve birch allergy for at least 25 weeks
lead.deck: In 97 birch pollen-allergic adults randomized double-blind against placebo, DM-101PX, a recombinant birch allergen modified to curb histamine release, reduced nasal symptoms triggered by allergen challenge after just 10 weeks of subcutaneous treatment, with the effect still visible 25 weeks after the last injection, a strong rise in allergen-specific IgG4 and good tolerability (no treatment-related discontinuations, every participant reaching the top dose). Where conventional desensitization runs for several years, the Espoo biotech, backed by a €28M raise in October, is preparing a dose-finding study and then aims for a licensing deal, M&A or an IPO.

milestone.title: NICE recommends Ekterly (sebetralstat), the first oral on-demand treatment for hereditary angioedema attacks, for the NHS in England and Wales
milestone.summary: In final draft guidance, the UK health technology assessor backs the oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor from KalVista, now part of Italy's Chiesi Group, for patients aged 12 and older. In the Phase 3 KONFIDENT trial, median time to onset of symptom relief was 1.61 hours with 300 mg sebetralstat versus 6.72 hours on placebo; the most common side effect was headache (9.2%).
milestone.why: Until now, a hereditary angioedema attack was treated by injection or infusion: a tablet taken at the first symptoms changes care for the UK's 1,000 to 1,500 patients. The same day, Dutch company Pharming paused production of Ruconest, its injectable attack treatment: the shift to oral therapy is squeezing the disease's incumbents.

deal.thesis: US-based Schrödinger is buying this 's-Hertogenbosch company, founded by Nicola Bonzanni, for about €22M in cash; its software automates analysis of antibody repertoire sequencing data and ranks candidates with machine learning, and the deal closed the same day. The physics-based simulation specialist thus links upstream biologics discovery to its LiveDesign for Biologics optimization tool: a sign that consolidation of the software building blocks of AI for antibodies has begun, at a price that remains modest for a European platform.

brefsEurope.title: Pharming pauses Ruconest production after a failed sterile fill test at its contract manufacturer and warns the FDA of a possible shortage
brefsEurope.summary: An aseptic process simulation (media fill) failed at the fill-finish subcontractor; production will resume only once the root cause is fixed and the process requalified, and stock covers the US market only until mid-December. Ruconest accounts for about 80% of revenue ($93.8M in the third quarter): shares fell 14.6% in Amsterdam.

brefsEurope.title: Bayer will pull Kerendia from the German market in mid-December, failing to secure an economically acceptable price
brefsEurope.summary: In October, the G-BA found no added benefit for finerenone in heart failure with an ejection fraction ≥ 40%; because the AMNOG system sets a single price across all indications, that also drags down reimbursement in chronic kidney disease. A signal for any European biotech targeting Germany, whose prices serve as a benchmark for other countries.

brefsEurope.title: Xbrane grants Hong Kong Yongtao Pharmaceutical an exclusive license to Ximluci, its ranibizumab biosimilar, in Greater China
brefsEurope.summary: Yongtao funds registration, market access and commercialization in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, while Xbrane keeps manufacturing; $2M upfront if China's NMPA requires no local study, none otherwise, with profit sharing in both cases. NMPA feedback is expected in Q1 2027, with a filing targeted for Q2.

brefsEurope.title: Valneva delays the next trial of its S4V2 Shigella vaccine while awaiting $143M in Pfizer payments tied to its Lyme disease vaccine
brefsEurope.summary: A new Phase 2 is meant to optimize dosing and schedule after two encouraging but insufficiently consistent trials; it will wait on regulatory progress for LB6V, whose next three Pfizer milestones depend on first sales in Europe and the US. Cash fell to €85.2M at end-September, and LimmaTech (now part of Lilly) can take back rights in low- and middle-income countries if no global health partner is found by the end of Phase 2.

brefsEurope.title: Zelluna proposes Adrian Woolfson (ex-Sangamo, Replay founder) as chair and Nerida Scott (ex-J&J Innovation EMEA) for its board
brefsEurope.summary: The Norwegian biotech develops allogeneic NK cells armed with a T-cell receptor (TCR-NK), including ZI-MA4-1 against MAGE-A4 in solid tumors. An extraordinary general meeting on December 18 is due to approve two business development-savvy profiles, with co-founder Anders Tuv staying on as a director.

brefsEurope.title: Bayer pays China's Hansoh $150M upfront for HS-20122, a Phase 1 EGFR × c-MET bispecific ADC, in a deal worth up to $3.25B
brefsEurope.summary: Exclusive global license outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, with up to $3.1B in milestones plus royalties, subject to antitrust clearance; the first target indication is non-small cell lung cancer. A comparable: Europe's big drugmakers keep sourcing early ADCs from China rather than from the continent's biotechs.

brefsEurope.title: Fluicell launches a fully guaranteed SEK 13.7M rights issue to commercialize its Nexocyte bioprinting platform
brefsEurope.summary: Subscription commitments of about 34% (chair, CEO and shareholders) with Aqurat underwriting the rest; subscription runs December 7–21. Net proceeds, estimated at SEK 11.3M, will fund commercialization of AI-supported heart tissue models for drug screening and its type 1 diabetes collaborations.

brefsIntl.title: FDA approves Cogent's Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumors after imatinib
brefsIntl.summary: In the PEAK trial, the combination extended median progression-free survival to 16.5 months versus 9.2 months on sunitinib alone (50% lower risk), with a 46% versus 26% response rate. Cogent's first drug, it opens up second-line GIST, where GSK is readying its KIT inhibitor velzatinib, in Phase 3.

word.definition: A treatment that gives small, rising doses of the offending allergen (pollen, peanut, dust mites…) to retrain the immune system so it stops overreacting, rather than merely masking symptoms.

parts.label: Allergen
parts.role: the target, natural or recombinant, sometimes modified to be less reactive

how.t: From the first doses, mast cells and basophils release less histamine, even before antibodies change.
Allergen-specific regulatory T cells emerge and secrete IL-10 and TGF-β, which dampen the allergic response.
Specific IgG4 rises and captures the allergen before it reaches IgE, whose levels decline slowly over months or years.

word.why: It is the only treatment able to change the course of allergy, but it remains demanding (years of regular dosing) and can trigger reactions with natural extracts. Modified recombinant allergens, peptides and patches promise shorter, safer courses: Desentum just showed a lasting effect after ten weeks, and DBV is awaiting the FDA on its peanut patch. A niche long overlooked by VCs, where proof of durability can trigger licensing or M&A.

startups.name: Desentum
startups.use: Modified recombinant birch allergen DM-101PX: positive Phase 2 BASIT in November 2026 after 10 weeks of treatment; peanut and cat programs in preclinical

startups.name: Aravax
startups.use: PVX108, a peptide mix mimicking the T-cell epitopes of peanut allergens, with no whole protein; positive Phase 2 in children and FDA Fast Track designation

startups.name: DBV Technologies
startups.use: Epicutaneous immunotherapy with the Viaskin Peanut patch: BLA filed with the FDA in September 2026 for children aged 4 to 7, after the Phase 3 VITESSE trial
